resources.string: %d min a day across all Vault apps
One allowance shared by every Vault app, so hopping from one to another doesn\'t dodge it. A smaller budget applies at once; a bigger one waits 24 hours.
Saved. A bigger budget applies in 24 hours; see Pending changes.
What matters today? Put the most important first: home shows the top three still to do.
A home screen that helps you use your phone less.
Distracting apps go in the Vault. They leave your home screen and search, and each open starts with a short pause that grows through the day.
One daily budget covers every Vault app. Making a rule stricter is instant; making it looser waits 24 hours.
Nothing you do leaves your phone, and there\'s no account. Only the weather line goes online, and only once you switch it on.

resources.string: Tick the apps that eat your time. Common ones are already ticked, and their websites go in the Vault with them. You can add more later in Settings, at once; taking one out waits 24 hours.
How many minutes a day, across all Vault apps together? You can lower it at any time. Raising it later waits 24 hours.
Choose which apps are tools, which pause to breathe first and which go in the Vault. Uninstall apps here too.
Lock button, battery, alarm, music, weather, the status bar, and what each tap and swipe does

Tool apps are always one search away. Breathe apps stay on home and in search, but every open starts with a short breathing pause: no time limit, and nothing taken from your budget. Vault apps leave home and search, open only when you type their full name, and share the daily budget. Hidden apps never show. Long-press an app\'s name to see its info or uninstall it.
Limit changes to %1$d a day in %2$s
Pause goes back to the usual in %s
How long it pauses before it opens. A longer pause applies at once; a shorter one waits 24 hours. A mode stricter than none can make it longer, never shorter.

A website in the Vault gets the same pause, budget and rules in Chrome, Firefox, Samsung Internet, Brave and other browsers, so switching to the browser isn\'t a way round. Adding one applies at once; taking one out waits 24 hours.
That isn\'t a web address. Try something like youtube.com.
Hours when Vault apps don\'t open at all
Which apps open during a focus session
A sticker or printed code that ends a block
Things to do instead, offered when you answer Bored or Habit
Press Enter to save. It comes back in your inbox at the end of a focus session and with the evening digest.
Nothing saved for later. Swipe left on home to capture a thought.
Nothing here. Updates held since the last digest come out at the next one.
Non-urgent notifications wait and arrive together three times a day, at 9:00, 14:00 and 20:00. Calls, alarms and the apps you tick below always come through straight away.
Needs notification access, and permission to post the summary

Each mode has its own budget and waits, and can let only chosen apps open. Turn one on here until a time you choose, or give it a schedule; either way it ends by itself. Switching to a stricter mode applies at once. Ending one early, or switching to a looser one, waits 24 hours.
Each mode turns on during its own hours
Then it ends by itself and the schedules take over. A later end applies at once; ending it sooner, or switching to a looser mode, waits 24 hours.
There\'s already a mode called that
It\'s on now or has hours that make things stricter, so removing it waits 24 hours; see Pending changes.
Switching to %1$s waits %2$s, past the %3$s end you picked. Apply it sooner or cancel it in Pending changes.
Minutes a day across all Vault apps
Saved. It makes the mode looser, so it applies in 24 hours; see Pending changes.
Inside a schedule, Vault apps are blocked. Only your physical key or an emergency pass gets past. A new or longer schedule applies at once; a shorter one, or removing it, waits 24 hours.
On: no Vault apps for an hour after the day\'s first unlock
Off. Tap to keep Vault apps shut for the first hour of each day.
Switches off in %s. Tap to keep it on.
Only your focus apps open. Do Not Disturb goes on, and the screen goes grey if grayscale is set up.
Lock it: ending early needs your key
Other apps open again straight away.
This session is locked. Ending it early needs your key.

During a focus session only these open. Anything else, Tool apps included, is blocked: an unlocked session lets you in after a 2-minute wait, a locked one only with your key. Calls always get through.

Pair a cheap NFC sticker or print a code, then leave it in another room or at work. A scheduled block or a locked focus session ends early only with a tap or a scan. Adding a key applies at once; removing one waits 24 hours.
Hold the sticker to the back of the phone.
Turn on NFC in the phone\'s settings, then hold your sticker to the back of the phone.
That sticker is already paired. Try another one.
Print this or save a screenshot, then keep it out of reach. It\'s shown only once; the app keeps only a fingerprint of it.
This key stops working in 24 hours. You can cancel that under Pending changes.
When you answer Bored or Habit on the pause screen, it offers one of these first, taking turns. Link an app to open it; otherwise Do this instead goes home.
Nothing here yet, so the pause screen won\'t offer anything instead.
While a Vault app is open
%s. Tap to switch between Off, While a Vault app is open, and Always.
Needs a one-time grant from a computer. Tap for how.
What the app needs and why

Sees which app comes to the front, so a Vault app opened from a notification, recents or another app still gets the pause screen. It reads what\'s on screen only where a rule you switched on needs it: inside an app with a blocked feed, a browser\'s address bar while a website is in the Vault, and Settings pages during a lock period. Nothing is stored or leaves the phone.
Installed outside the Play Store? Android 13 and later grey out this setting until you open app info, tap ⋮ and choose Allow restricted settings.

Android\'s Advanced Protection is on. It takes accessibility away from apps that aren\'t accessibility tools, this one included. Lite protection takes over once usage access and display over other apps are on.

Without accessibility, checks once a second which app is in front, so a Vault app opened from a notification or recents still gets the pause and its time still counts. Nothing on screen is read, so feed blocking, website rules and the lock guard stay off.
Lets the pause screen open on top of a Vault app when accessibility is off.
Every unlock lands here, so Vault apps aren\'t one tap away.
Stops the system from pausing the app in the background, which would switch protection off.
Turns the screen grey while a Vault app is open, which makes feeds less gripping. Android lets only a computer grant this: turn on USB debugging, connect the phone and run the command below once.

For the digest: holds non-urgent notifications and releases them three times a day. They stay on the phone. Installed outside the Play Store? Allow restricted settings in app info first, as for accessibility.
Lets the digest post its one summary, and tells you when a new app goes into the Vault.
Shows your next calendar item under the clock. Nothing else is read.
Turns on Do Not Disturb during focus sessions and puts it back afterwards.

Notices when a Vault app comes to the front so the pause screen can appear first. Screen content is read only where a rule you switched on needs it, such as a blocked feed inside YouTube, a browser\'s address bar for a Vault website, or Settings during a lock period. Nothing is stored and nothing leaves the phone.
Making a rule stricter applies at once. Making it looser waits 24 hours, so a weak moment can\'t undo a calm decision. You can cancel a waiting change at any time.
Shut the endless parts of apps, keep the useful ones

When a blocked feed comes on screen, the app steps back out of it. Search, messages and the rest keep working. Switching a block on applies at once; switching it off waits 24 hours. Apps change their screens now and then, so a block can stop working until it\'s updated.
Switches off in %s. Tap to keep it on.
%s is switched off. The rest of the app still works.
Switch to the app; its node tree goes to logcat (tag ScreenDump)
Lock every setting for 7, 30 or 90 days

During a lock nothing can be loosened at all: no bigger budget, no apps out of the Vault, no rules switched off, and no skipping waits with a friend code, typing or a key. Tightening still works. Changes already waiting apply only once the lock ends. A lock can be made longer but never shorter.
Until %s nothing can be loosened. This can\'t be undone or shortened.
Locked until %s. Nothing can be loosened until then.
Not saved: a lock period is on.
Locked until %s. These wait until the lock ends.
Skip the rest of the wait with one of these. Each is meant to take some effort, so a weak moment still costs something.
Codes a friend keeps, to skip a wait

Make 10 one-time codes and send them to a friend. When you want a waiting change to apply now, ask them to read you one. Each code works once. The app keeps only fingerprints of them, and this screen can\'t be screenshotted.
Make 10 new codes (the old ones stop working)
These are shown only once. Send them to your friend now.
Please keep these codes for me. When I ask, read me one, but only if you think I really mean it. Each works once.
Ask your friend to read you one of the codes.
That isn\'t one of the codes, or it was used already.
While this is on, Android won\'t uninstall Enough until you switch it off. Enough asks for no other device controls.
Switching this off lets Enough be uninstalled. During a lock period, this page is blocked.
Android won\'t uninstall the app while this is on. During a lock period the app also keeps you out of its own App info, device admin and accessibility pages, so it can\'t be switched off from there.
Enough makes cheating take effort. It can\'t make it impossible, and it won\'t pretend to:
Safe mode starts the phone without any downloaded app, this one included.
A factory reset wipes everything, rules and all.
A computer with USB debugging can switch off or uninstall any app.
Changing the phone\'s clock is ignored while the phone stays on, but not across a restart.
Feed blocking, website rules and the uninstall guard read other apps\' screens. When those apps change their design, a rule can stop working until it\'s updated.
Some phones stop background apps to save battery. Allowing unrestricted battery on the next screen helps.
The point is a pause between the urge and the app, not a cage.
This week against last. Opens once a day.
Come back tomorrow. The report opens once a day, so checking it doesn\'t become a habit of its own.

Bedtime: Sleep mode, grey screen, only calls, alarm and a book

From 30 minutes before bedtime until you wake, the Sleep mode is on: no Vault apps, the screen goes grey (if grayscale is set up), and only calls, the alarm clock and an e-book app open. The first unlock after waking lands on Today. Setting it up applies at once; switching it off or loosening it waits 24 hours.
That makes bedtime looser, so it applies in %s. See Pending changes.

Android 15 can keep apps in a Private space that the system itself locks behind your screen lock. For a hard, OS-level lock, install your worst Vault apps there (from the Private space\'s own Play Store). While it\'s locked, its apps are hidden everywhere in Enough.
There\'s no Private space on this phone. Set one up in the phone\'s Settings under Security and privacy, then come back.
Enough uses Android\'s accessibility service to put a pause in front of the apps you chose. It isn\'t an accessibility tool for disabilities.
It sees which app is in front, so a Vault app opened from a notification, recents or a link still gets the pause screen, and its time counts against your budget.

It reads what\'s on screen only where a rule you switched on needs it: the endless feed inside an app you blocked it in, a browser\'s address bar while a website is in the Vault, and this app\'s own Settings pages during a lock period. It looks only for those, and keeps none of what it reads.
It can press Back or Home to leave a blocked feed or page, lock the screen when you double-tap home or tap the lock, and pull down notifications when you swipe down on home.
Nothing it sees is stored beyond which app was open and for how long, and none of it leaves the phone.
Switch parts of home on or off. Changes apply at once.
A lock icon at the bottom right of home, within reach of your thumb. Tap it to lock the phone. Double-tapping empty space on home does the same.
Locking needs the accessibility service, which is off. Tap to turn it on.

When your next alarm goes off, if one is set. Tap it on home to open your alarms.
What\'s playing in Spotify, YouTube Music or any other player, with Previous, Pause and Next. Tap the song to open the player.

An estimate of the US air quality index and PM2.5 where you are. It comes from a forecast model (CAMS, through Open-Meteo) that covers about 45 km and averages over 24 hours, so it can read well below sensor sites such as aqi.in, especially in Indian cities. Tap it on home to refresh.
Weather and air quality need your location. Tap to allow it.

Weather and air quality are the only parts of Enough that use the internet. They come from Open-Meteo, which is sent your rough location, rounded to about a kilometre, and nothing else. Both stay off until you switch them on.
